findings.reason: §6 claims every writer that can race the landing write "either commutes or refuses", but the SPA/HTTP writer is a second implementation of the same contract and is neither fenced nor named, so the plan should route `serve.py:_handle_plan_write` through the store's fenced write path (or have it take the same `plans` lock/namespace) rather than fence only half the contract.
findings.text: `_handle_plan_write` performs its own read-check-replace (`serve.py:3519` read, `3542` check, `3610-3612` write to a fixed `.html.tmp`) without the store's `plans` lock, so a writer arriving by `POST /plan/<project>/<slug>` can pass its version check, move another writer's rendered file into place and be lost with the counter advanced — the §1 defect and the §5 fixed-`.tmp` collision, reproduced on the one plan-write path §6 does not enumerate

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is added; the lock, the commutative merge and the refusal shape live inside `reckon/_store.py`, `reckon/_plan_html.py` and `reckon/mcp.py` behind their existing `edit_plan`/`write_plan` entry points, so the added behaviour sits behind an interface no larger than before.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan fences `reckon/_store.py`'s plan write but leaves the second implementation of the same versioned plan-write contract in `reckon/serve.py:3462` unfenced, so the owner to extend is the store and the HTTP route is not routed through it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design extends the fence the store already holds (`reckon/_store.py:_serialized_path_lock`, reused under the "plans" namespace) and names its rival helpers — S13's `resolve_both.py` and the existing `edit_plan` version check it is not rebuilding.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan proposes no wrapper; each section extends an existing op (append, set, text mode, the conflict refusal helper `reckon/mcp.py:_conflict_response`) rather than layering a parallel call over it.
